_readme: Real photos TAKEN BY the machines in the game (not photos of them). Each caption comes from the NASA description at `source`; keep captions <= 25 words. Only NASA/JPL(-Caltech) credits are used: images co-credited to universities or companies (Cassini/SSI, New Horizons/JHUAPL/SwRI, LRO/ASU, Blue Ghost/Firefly) are skipped per CLAUDE.md rule 4 until the team decides. Apollo photos are skipped (taken by astronauts, not the hardware). Files live in assets/photos/ and are also listed in assets/manifest.json.

photos.title: The first photo from the surface of Mars
photos.caption: The first photograph ever taken on the surface of Mars, minutes after Viking 1 landed. Rocks, sand and dust.

photos.title: Morning on Chryse Planitia
photos.caption: A wide view of Chryse Planitia in the morning, stitched together from Viking Lander 1's camera 1.

photos.title: Opportunity's shadow
photos.caption: Opportunity caught its own shadow with its front hazard-avoidance camera while driving into Endurance Crater.

photos.title: A long shadow at Endeavour Crater
photos.caption: Opportunity's afternoon shadow stretching into Endeavour Crater, on its 3,051st day on Mars.

photos.title: InSight's first selfie
photos.caption: InSight's first selfie on Mars: its solar panels and deck, with its science instruments on top.
photos.camera: InSight, Instrument Deployment Camera on its robotic arm

photos.title: Sunset on Mars
photos.caption: A sunset on Mars, taken with the camera on the end of InSight's robotic arm.

photos.title: InSight's final selfie
photos.caption: InSight's last selfie. Its solar panels are covered with far more dust than in its first one.

photos.title: Ingenuity's shadow on its first flight
photos.caption: Ingenuity photographed its own shadow while hovering, during the first powered, controlled flight on another planet.

photos.title: The first color photo of Mars from the air
photos.caption: The first color image of Mars taken by an aircraft while flying, during Ingenuity's second flight.

photos.title: Earth and Moon together
photos.caption: A crescent Earth and Moon in one picture, the first of its kind taken by a spacecraft. Voyager 1 was 7.25 million miles away.

photos.title: The Pale Blue Dot
photos.caption: Earth as a tiny point of light, seen from more than 4 billion miles away. Part of the first portrait of the solar system.

photos.title: Uranus
photos.caption: The planet Uranus, photographed by Voyager 2 as it flew past.

photos.title: Neptune
photos.caption: Neptune in enhanced color, taken as Voyager 2 closed in on the planet.
